chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdullah al-Barqi, raising it from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abu Abdullah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about selling the spinning yarn with the expanded fabric, and the spinning yarn is more in weight than the clothes. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem'.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell raw yarn for finished clothes if the yarn weighs more than the clothes?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by the prominent scholar al-Barqi, this hadith clarifies the permissibility of exchanging raw materials for finished goods despite weight reduction during processing, a key nuance in Shia commercial jurisprudence. It demonstrates the Imam's practical approach to trade, distinguishing between the intrinsic value of the material and the physical changes incurred through labor, thereby validating such barter as free from riba (usury) or defect.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abu Abdullah Al Barqy, raising it from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about selling the spinning yarn with the expanded fabric, and the spinning yarn is more in weight than the clothes. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu ‘Abd Allah al-Barqiy in a marfu’ manner from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of exchanging yarns for expanded fabrics while the yarn is heavier than fabrics in weight. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
